output.reason: The CRD validator confirms that the object-level default of spec.metadataOptions changed only httpPutResponseHopLimit, from 2 to 1 [ev-8998581760b8][ev-451bd6a12e72]. Nothing in the evidence says anything fails or is rejected, so behavior-change (review) is the right kind. However, the proposed statement says any object that leaves httpPutResponseHopLimit unset now gets 1. The validator refuted that: the sub-field's own default in the target schema is still 2. Only objects that leave spec.metadataOptions unset entirely are affected, so I corrected the statement's scope.

correction.statement: In the karpenter.k8s.aws/v1beta1 EC2NodeClass schema, the default of spec.metadataOptions now sets httpPutResponseHopLimit to 1 instead of 2 (other entries unchanged). v1beta1 EC2NodeClass objects that leave spec.metadataOptions unset get hop limit 1; this is a behavior change to review.

consequence.statement: v1beta1 EC2NodeClass objects that leave spec.metadataOptions unset now get the default httpPutResponseHopLimit 1 instead of 2. The httpEndpoint "enabled", httpProtocolIPv6 "disabled" and httpTokens "required" defaults are unchanged. Objects that set spec.metadataOptions but omit httpPutResponseHopLimit still get the field-level default of 2.
consequence.remediation: If a hop limit of 2 is needed, set spec.metadataOptions explicitly on the EC2NodeClass, including httpPutResponseHopLimit: 2.
